prompt: A 1990s article predicts that email will flatten every company's hierarchy, simply because of what email is.
tells: simply because of what email is
why: Technology alone is said to cause the outcome.
trap: Affordance would ask what it makes possible for whom.

prompt: A consultancy report says AI will inevitably replace middle managers, whatever firms decide to do with it.
tells: whatever firms decide to do with it
trap: The report may become self-fulfilling, but its claim is determinist.

prompt: A survey study measures 'the impact of the system' on productivity, treating the system as the cause and staff behavior as the effect.
tells: treating the system as the cause and staff behavior as the effect
why: A one-way causal model from tech to people.
trap: Sociotechnical systems balance two subsystems; this has one causing the other.

prompt: A pop-history book says the printing press, by itself, produced the scientific revolution.
tells: by itself, produced the scientific revolution
trap: No model is being acted on.

prompt: A vendor promises that installing their collaboration suite will create a culture of openness within six months.
tells: installing their collaboration suite will create a culture of openness
why: The tool is claimed to cause the culture.
trap: The vendor might also be enrolling the buyer, but the claim is determinist.

prompt: A manager says productivity fell because of the new video tool, and that nothing the teams did could have changed that.
tells: nothing the teams did could have changed that
why: The tool alone is said to cause the outcome.
trap: A constraint leaves room for people to respond; this claim leaves none.
